People likely experienced weak shaking there.
Many smaller towns and villages are located closer to the epicenter and might have experienced stronger shaking.

No aftershocks have been recorded so far.
When aftershocks are detected, we will update this section.

Larger earthquakes (above magnitude 5 or so) such as this one are usually followed by smaller ones known as **aftershocks** that occur in the same area during the days, weeks, months or even years after the main shock.
Based on its magnitude, the fault that was active during the quake likely **ruptured beneath a surface area of approximately 4 km 2 (2 square miles)** as a first-order estimate.
The length of the rupture zone thus was probably around 3 km (2 mi).
